obfuscation_features: runtime string literals partially preserved for build-time tractability

task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after staged UI gating, custom-event dispatch, tuple preparation and asynchronous continuation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: four-stage DOM click gate (calibrate, arm, preview, collect) plus two CustomEvent hops (stage and collect), promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and mutation-observer continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The fingerprint value is carried through an arm/preview/collect staged scan-session flow before the sink wrapper receives it.
The selected slot and config are recovered through a runtime table before the converter is called.

The click path crosses staged session gating, custom event dispatch, action routing, signal filtering, scan-mode projection, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, middleware, slot config selection, fingerprint byte materialization and console sink wrapping.
Dozens of decoy modules call the same factory with non-target slots, so nearby factory usage is not enough to identify the target anchor.
The UI signal scan remains semantically plausible, but the target observable is the browser_fp field on the fingerprint collect output rather than visual signal listing or preview state.
The target value is separated from the scan click by arm and preview state, CustomEvent dispatch, Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The final sink receives an already encoded fp_ fingerprint, so sink inspection alone cannot identify the construction site.
The converter receives tuple rows plus transit, scan-mode, extended-signal and statistics context that were prepared in earlier layers.

behavior_category.subtype: staged signal-collection browser fingerprint hash derivation
behavior_category.reason: The observable value is derived by composing collected browser signal tuple lanes, materializing an 18-byte Uint8Array from the staged scan configuration, runtime transit state and statistics, then folding it into a stable fp_ console fingerprint hash.

near_categories.why_not: The byte materialization is an intermediate stage; the observable target is a browser fingerprint hash string, not a typed-array payload.
The anchor mixes collected browser signals into a fingerprint digest rather than only formatting state fields.
The output has no request proof, token or seal semantics.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten.
